assets.issues: Video: Premier League Classics： Arsenal v. Tottenham Hotspur ｜ FULL MATCH ｜ 12⧸2⧸2018 ｜ NBC Sports [D29dNXViqJw].mp4. Pregame starting-XI graphic is very clean and fully legible at 52-79s; strongest non-live exposure in the audit.
assets.suggestions: Keep this asset class prominent: retain flat graphic treatment, generous clear space, and center-weighted layout. If extended, add a slightly thicker red outline/shadow so it stays crisp on smaller mobile screens.

assets.issues: Tottenham shirt-front sponsor appears throughout the match and is usually fully legible, but weakest moments occur when players turn away or are mid-stride: 1499-1501s (partially legible, back/angled view of Eriksen), 1621-1623s (partially legible during duel), 1672-1675s (partially legible in aerial challenge), 1683-1693s (partially legible in moving close-up of Kane). Stronger hero moments include 1155-1161s, 1170-1178s, 1200-1206s, 1735-1737s, 1941-1955s.
assets.suggestions: Very effective overall. To improve edge cases, enlarge the wordmark height slightly or add a darker keyline around red letters so the sponsor survives torso twist, folds, and partial occlusion in action shots.

assets.issues: Bench/fascia AIA appears only briefly and in background close-ups around 3808-3815s and 6069-6083s. Fully legible, but secondary and easy to miss.
assets.suggestions: If bench branding is meant to carry weight, increase panel scale and place it directly behind seated coach eyelines; avoid low-slung placements that sit below the editorial focal point.

assets.issues: Training-kit AIA appears once around 5128-5134s and is background-only.
assets.suggestions: Use larger benchwear marks or repeat the logo on outerwear/chest zones most likely to face camera during manager/staff reactions.

brands.name: AIA
brands.summary: Best-performing brand in the broadcast. It wins on volume and editorial context: pregame graphic plus 118 shirt-front hits across open play, close-ups, celebrations, halftime, substitutions, and postgame. Weakness is not contrast but orientation/motion when players rotate or sprint.

assets.issues: Nike appears as Tottenham kit manufacturer logo. Because the swoosh is small, it loses legibility faster than shirt sponsors. Weak examples: 2342-2345s (mostly legible, player down on turf), 4327-4330s (mostly legible during touchline duel). Better examples: 88-91s pregame, 167-169s, 281-287s.
assets.suggestions: Increase logo scale slightly or add stronger contrast separation from fabric texture. The current chest-scale mark is too small for moving match coverage; a brighter outline/embroidery edge would help.

assets.issues: Nike also appears on bench/training apparel around 4853-4856s in a close-up and reads better than the on-kit swoosh because of steadier framing.
assets.suggestions: Benchwear execution is stronger; prioritize camera-facing staff outerwear with larger chest placement for more dependable broadcast pickup.

brands.name: Nike
brands.summary: Creatively clean but broadcast-limited by scale. The logo is recognizable in close-ups, yet often too small to carry value in motion-heavy play.

assets.issues: Emirates perimeter LED is the most consistently readable board brand in the match, spanning pregame, open play, replay, and goal contexts. Even in wide play it stays fully legible: 102-130s, 162-167s, 194-208s, 1501-1528s, 1659-1672s, 1712-1737s, 1850-1929s. Main limitation is distance rather than readability.
assets.suggestions: Already strong. For extra standout in the widest camera, increase letter height or shorten copy cycles so the mark is centered during attacking-third action.

assets.issues: Arsenal shirt-front sponsor is strong in player close-ups and celebrations: 217-220s, 248-256s, multiple goal/celebration hits later in match. No poor metadata examples were flagged; weaknesses are mainly occasional partial folds when players twist.
assets.suggestions: Maintain current white-on-red/white kit approach. A slightly thicker letter weight would help in fast tracking shots, but this is already premium broadcast inventory.

assets.issues: Stadium fascia/signage performs well from the opening hero shot 0-11s and later wide or celebration cuts (including 1011-1048s and 1948-1951s). Always fully legible in metadata, though naturally secondary to play.
assets.suggestions: Lean into opening, goal, and crowd-reaction framing with repeated fascia blocks near camera-facing stands. This is valuable emotional-context inventory that conventional play-only audits undercount.

brands.name: Emirates
brands.summary: One of the strongest all-around brands: excellent home-team shirt visibility plus frequent, clean perimeter and stadium signage exposure. Strong across both live action and emotional context shots.

assets.issues: Betfair appears only on perimeter LED but with solid volume across open play and replay. Weakest render is 583-599s (mostly legible in midfield wide shot). Better moments: 599-648s around the foul/free-kick buildup, 669-745s replays, 752-817s resumption. QA suggests distance, lower-frame placement, and player obstruction are the main issues.
assets.suggestions: Increase luminance separation between text and board background, and avoid keeping the wordmark too low in frame. A bolder white/yellow lockup or tighter copy block would survive wide-camera distance better.

brands.name: Betfair
brands.summary: Good frequency, but creative effectiveness is capped by standard wide-shot LED conditions. Works best on stoppage/replay sequences when the camera settles.

assets.issues: 12BET appears on both stadium signage and perimeter LED. Stadium signage at 433-443s is clean. Perimeter LED delivers long runs later in match, but weaker examples include 4738-4752s during the Arsenal goal sequence and 4779-4789s replay, where metadata drops to mostly legible. Distance and foreground player clutter reduce clarity.
assets.suggestions: Improve wide-shot pickup with larger numeral/letter proportions and more negative space. The red/white-on-dark palette is decent, but a stronger white border/glow would help against crowd and player clutter.

assets.issues: Stadium fascia exposure at 433-443s is fully legible but brief and secondary.
assets.suggestions: Repeat fascia units more densely or place them closer to dugout/throw-in camera positions for longer incidental visibility.

brands.name: 12BET
brands.summary: Moderate creative performance. The brand has useful later-match LED volume, but readability softens in the biggest moments because of wide angles and foreground interference.

assets.issues: Lexus performs best as a broadcast graphic/bug rather than as an in-stadium asset. Strong moments: 2587-2589s top-frame graphic and 5959-5979s stoppage-time bug. Always fully legible because it is screen-native.
assets.suggestions: Keep using overlay inventory. To maximize value, hold the bug a touch longer and anchor it slightly farther from the extreme corner so it is less ignorable on mobile crops.

assets.issues: Scorebug/substitution integration at 2882-2883s and 3090-3103s is fully legible but small and peripheral.
assets.suggestions: Enlarge sponsor lockup within the scorebug package or give it a brief animated reveal during substitutions/stoppage announcements to command more attention.

brands.name: Lexus
brands.summary: High-quality but low-volume exposure. Lexus benefits from clean broadcast-native graphics, though the asset is small and peripheral rather than immersive.

assets.issues: Gatorade perimeter LED is fully legible whenever shown, including 373-377s and later replay/wide-shot moments. Frequency is limited. Background usage means it rarely dominates the frame.
assets.suggestions: Good color separation already; improve impact by increasing logo scale or reducing ancillary copy so the icon/wordmark reads faster from the main wide camera.

assets.issues: Fascia/other placements are brief: 187-194s and 5451-5456s. They are readable but incidental.
assets.suggestions: Shift background placements nearer benches, tunnel, or substitution zones where editorial cutaways linger; current placements are visible but not memorable.

brands.name: Gatorade
brands.summary: Limited but tidy presence. Creative holds up technically, yet lack of scale and editorial focus keep total impact moderate.

assets.issues: BYD perimeter LED is clean around the penalty/goal sequence: 683-698s plus replays 726-738s. Strong emotional-context usage boosts value. No poor-render examples flagged in metadata.
assets.suggestions: Continue owning high-attention moments, but increase board brightness consistency during replay packages so the brand pops equally from alternate angles.

assets.issues: BYD is heavily present on bench/fascia/technical-area inventory: 97-102s pregame, 349-351s, 790-817s, 981-998s, and multiple later close-ups. This off-ball exposure is valuable because it lands during manager reaction shots. Some placements are classified as 'other' or training-kit/bench signage rather than standard stadium boards.
assets.suggestions: This is a strong non-play asset. To maximize it, keep branding directly behind coaches and substitutes, and use repeated seat-back/bench-panel marks so every reaction shot carries the logo.

assets.issues: Training-kit/bench-seat BYD at 790-799s and 812-817s is clearly visible and benefits from stable close-up framing.
assets.suggestions: Preserve this exact placement strategy; it converts routine bench cutaways into high-quality sponsorship inventory.

brands.name: BYD
brands.summary: Best hidden-value brand in the audit. Beyond a short but useful goal-sequence LED run, BYD scores especially well in bench and technical-area close-ups that many standard reports miss.
